stories.title: LLSWS 2026 — Johnston County Returns Home as Champions

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Johnston County is going home.

North Carolina's four-time LLSWS champions are heading back to Clayton. Coach Ben Catarozzoli: "Can't take that feeling away, they've worked so hard."

2015. 2019. 2024. 2026. Champions. 🥎 #LLSWS #Softball #NorthCarolina

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
41 strikeouts in one tournament.

Anna-Lynn Clark pitched 20 of NC's 24 innings at the LLSWS, allowed 3 runs all week, and closed it with a CG shutout in the final.

That's one of the most dominant tournament pitching performances the LLSWS has ever seen. 🥎 #LLSWS #Softball

research.facts:
LLSWS 2026 — Johnston County Homecoming / Championship Legacy
**Sources:**
- WKML 95.7 / Foxy99 / 107.7 The Bounce / Sunny 94.3 — "Johnston County Gives NC Another Little League Softball World Series Title" (Aug 10, 2026)
- WITN.com — "Johnston County wins Softball LLWS" (Aug 9/10, 2026)
- MLB.com — "North Carolina wins 2026 Little League Softball World Series"
- Yahoo Sports — "Johnston County, NC wins LLSWS" (Aug 9/10, 2026)
- JoCo Report — "Johnston County Little League Wins Softball World Series Championship"
- ABC11 Raleigh-Durham — Championship game coverage
**Key Facts (HIGH confidence — multiple sources):**
- Final: North Carolina 2, Kentucky 0 (Aug 9, 2026)
- Venue: Stallings Stadium, Greenville, NC; broadcast: ABC
- Scoring: Belle Cox RBI single (2nd inning) scored Sophie Catarozzoli — 1-0 NC; Campbell Swearengin scored on Kentucky throwing error in 3rd — 2-0 NC (final)
- Anna-Lynn Clark: 93 pitches, CG shutout, 3 H, 6 K in championship game
- Clark did not allow any Kentucky runner past 2nd base in the final 5 innings
- Clark tournament totals: 41 strikeouts (most of any pitcher in the field), 20 of NC's 24 tournament innings pitched, 3 ER allowed across entire event
- Clark games with 10+ Ks: vs Lake Mary (pool, 13 K, CG shutout, 2 BB, 5 H); vs FL semifinal (109 pitches, 11 K, CG shutout)
- NC titles: 2015, 2019, 2024, 2026 — 4th all-time
- NC trails only Texas (14), Florida (8), California (5) all-time in LLSWS titles
- Coach: Ben Catarozzoli — full post-game quote: "Can't take that feeling away, they've worked so hard. We told them from day one if they continue to work the way they did and believe in each other, that we could accomplish this."
- Sophie Catarozzoli (scorer of 1st run) shares surname with coach — family connection
- Homecoming/celebration context: Community watch parties held in Johnston County during the game; formal parade/celebration being organized for team's return to Clayton, NC
- Local coverage: WKML 95.7, Sunny 94.3, 107.7 The Bounce, ABC11 Raleigh-Durham, JoCo Report
**Freshness:** Championship was Aug 9; recap angle ran Aug 10; today = homecoming/legacy/Clark's historical impact angle.

- JustWomensSports.com — All-Star Cup 2026 schedule and how to watch
**Key Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Series 1 ran Aug 8-10, Parkway Bank Sports Complex (The Stadium), Rosemont, IL
- Series 1 captains: Rachel Garcia, Keilani Ricketts, Georgina Corrick
- Format: 3-team round-robin = 3 games in Series 1 (Aug 8/9/10)
- Game 1 (Aug 8, Saturday): Team Garcia won; Sami Williams 2-RBI double in 3rd inning (decisive blow); MVP-1: Sami Williams (+60 pts, 190 total); MVP-2: Karlyn Pickens (+40 pts); MVP-3: Sharlize Palacios (+20 pts)
- Game 2 (Aug 9, Sunday): Team Corrick won 4-3; Megan Grant hit a grand slam (decisive blow)
- Game 3 / Series 1 Finale (Aug 10, Monday, 7 PM ET on ESPNU): Team Ricketts won 2-0 over Team Garcia
- Kayla Kowalik (2025 champion, .486 BA, 1,590 pts) sat out all of Series 1
- After Series 1, top 3 individual point earners become Series 2 captains; teams fully redrafted
- Kowalik re-enters competition in Series 2 (week of Aug 11+)
- Broadcast: ESPN, ESPNU, MLB Network, CBS Sports Network
**Freshness:** Series 1 concluded Aug 10. Today = first day of the transition between Series 1 and Series 2.
